technical_body.formula: capacity_bytes = floor(W * H * len(channels) * bits_per_channel / 8) - header_overhead

variables.header_overhead: ST3GG v3 header (~48 bytes) + optional 4-byte length prefix + AES-GCM 16-byte tag if encrypted

technical_body.worked_example: 1920×1080 RGB @ 1 bpc → 1920*1080*3/8 = 777,600 bytes raw; ~777,552 usable after header.
technical_body.notes: Doubling bits_per_channel doubles capacity but increases statistical detectability (chi-square rate grows super-linearly).

technical_body.formula: capacity_bits = sum over adjacent pixel pairs (i, j) of floor(log2(range_width(|p_i - p_j|)))

variables.range_width: Wu–Tsai partitions the 0-255 difference space into sub-ranges (typically [0,7], [8,15], [16,31], [32,63], [64,127], [128,255]); wider ranges carry more bits
variables.adjacent: horizontal or vertical neighboring pixels in the traversal order

technical_body.worked_example: Uniform smooth image (all diffs in [0,7]) → 3 bits per pair. Edge-heavy image (diffs in [128,255]) → 7 bits per pair.
technical_body.notes: Data-dependent capacity; edge-rich carriers hide more. Pre-flight with img_core.pvd_capacity_bits before encoding.

technical_body.formula: capacity_bits = floor(W / block_size) * floor(H / block_size); usable_bytes = max(0, capacity_bits // 8 - 9)

variables.W, H: image width and height in pixels
variables.block_size: 8 by default (fixed for browser interop); configurable 1..32
variables.9 header bytes: DCTS magic (4) + strength byte (1) + big-endian u32 length (4)
variables.robustness: quantization step 10/25/50 for low/medium/high — controls per-bit visibility and re-encode survival but NOT capacity; ST3GG's dct_encode embeds one bit at coefficient position (0,1) of every 8×8 block regardless of robustness

technical_body.notes: ST3GG's img_core.dct_encode uses exactly one embedding position, (0,1), per 8×8 luminance block — matching the browser Text Lab DCT tool. Robustness picks how strongly to quantize that one coefficient (low=10, medium=25, high=50), not how many coefficients per block are used. Higher robustness survives more re-encoding at the cost of visible banding; capacity is invariant.

variables.|nonzero_AC_coefs|: count of non-zero AC DCT coefficients after quantization (highly Q-table-dependent)
variables.k: matrix-encoding parameter; typical range 1-4. k=1 collapses to LSB replacement; larger k trades capacity for fewer changes per bit.

technical_body.worked_example: 1920×1080 Q75 JPEG has ~500K nonzero AC coefs. At k=3: 500000 * 3/7 ≈ 214,000 bits ≈ 26 KB before shrinkage.
technical_body.notes: Shrinkage (coefficients decremented to 0 must be re-embedded) reduces effective capacity by ~5-10% on typical natural images. The k-vs-capacity tradeoff is F5's key innovation over jsteg.

variables.|nonzero_AC_coefs|: same as F5; typically ~500K on a 1920×1080 Q75 JPEG

technical_body.worked_example: 500K nonzero AC coefs → ~62 KB raw, ~62 KB minus 16-bit length prefix.
technical_body.notes: One bit per nonzero AC coefficient. Detected by chi-square (Westfeld-Pfitzmann 1999); the technique the attack was invented against.

technical_body.formula: capacity_bytes = unbounded (extends cover); stego_length = cover_length + 8 * payload_bytes + 2 (delimiters)

variables.payload_bytes: length of the plaintext payload in UTF-8 bytes
variables.cover_length: cover text is unmodified except for a trailing invisible run of ZWSP/ZWNJ codepoints

technical_body.worked_example: 100-byte payload → 802 zero-width codepoints appended to the cover (100*8 = 800 bits + 2 ZWJ delimiters).
technical_body.notes: No prefix scheme (delimiter-bracketed), so there's no capacity ceiling from the cover — the payload is appended. Dies to Unicode normalization and terminal glyph filtering.

variables.count_of_Latin_letters_in_cover: number of ASCII a-z / A-Z codepoints in the cover text
variables.-16: 16-bit LE length prefix consumes 16 carrier positions

technical_body.worked_example: Cover with 664 Latin letters → floor((664-16)/8) = 81 payload bytes.
technical_body.notes: Length-prefixed, so covers with < 16 Latin letters fail with a TextStegCapacityError before encoding starts.

variables.count_of_ASCII_punct_in_cover: count of , . ; : ! ? ( ) codepoints in the cover

technical_body.worked_example: Cover with 88 ASCII punctuation marks → floor((88-16)/8) = 9 payload bytes.
technical_body.notes: Cover selection is the practical constraint — most prose is letter-heavy, so CJK-homoglyph capacity is lower than cyrillic on the same text.

technical_body.formula: capacity_bytes = line_count - 2 (2 lines consumed by the 16-bit length prefix)

variables.line_count: number of lines with at least one trailing-whitespace slot in the cover

technical_body.notes: One byte per line (8 bits of trailing space/tab pattern). Dies wherever the receiver trims trailing whitespace.

technical_body.formula: capacity_bytes = unbounded (extends cover); stego_length = cover_length + payload_bytes + 2 (delimiters)

variables.payload_bytes: printable ASCII payload length; each byte maps 1:1 into a tag codepoint

technical_body.notes: One tag codepoint per payload byte. High capacity relative to zero-width (8× more bits per codepoint), but dies to more transports (Slack paste, LLM tokenizer normalizers).

variables.count_of_alnum_in_cover: count of alphanumeric codepoints in the cover (each can carry a bit)

technical_body.worked_example: Cover with 400 alphanumerics → floor((400-16)/8) = 48 payload bytes.
Cover with 320 alphabetic chars → floor((320-16)/8) = 38 payload bytes.

variables.count_of_ASCII_spaces_in_cover: count of U+0020 codepoints; each carries 2 bits by variant substitution
variables.-8: 16-bit length prefix consumes 8 spaces (2 bits each)

technical_body.worked_example: Cover with 200 ASCII spaces → floor((200-8)/4) = 48 payload bytes.
